2DT00.name: Delivering Results Together
2DT00.description: With the Quadrennial Comprehensive Policy Review serving as its mandate, the Delivering Results Together Fund (DRT-F) supported countries in the application of the Delivering as One approach for integrated policy and operational functions. Programme resources filled funding gaps and support tailored and collaborative action, no only increasing United Nations coherence at the country level, but strengthening links between the normative and operational aspects making development gains. Contributing to 2030 Agenda acceleration and the effective achievement of sustainable development results involved an integrated approach to policy change and the alignment of One Programmes with national priorities.

AL100.name: Albania SDG Acceleration Fund
AL100.description: The Albania SDG Acceleration Fund advances the 2030 Agenda by accelerating progress towards achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Stakeholders direct support to SDG priority areas of the National Strategy for Development and Integration (2015-2020) and the Programme of Cooperation for Sustainable Development (2017-2021).

CLH00.name: Haiti Cholera Response Multi-Partner Trust Fund
CLH00.description: Utilizing an integrated approach, the United Nations Haiti Cholera Response Multi-Partner Trust Fund provides quick and flexible financing for responses to cholera in Haiti. Initiatives are designed and implemented in accordance with the needs, requirements, and strategic objectives of a new approach to humanitarian programming and sustainable development.

DPS00.name: Darfur Community Peace and Stability Fund
DPS00.description: Established in 2007, the Darfur Community Peace and Stability Fund (DCPSF) promotes peacebuilding and reconciliation by implementing community-based recovery and development activities in Darfur. A pooled funding mechanism, the DCPSF channel funds to programmes addressing the most critical needs in the areas of social service delivery, peacebuilding, improved governance, and community livelihoods.

JCG30.name: JP DRC Sexual Violence Prevent
JCG30.description: As part of national stabilization and reconstruction efforts in Eastern Congo, the DRC Sexual Prevention Joint Programme was launched to respond to humanitarian and security needs linked to the increase in cases of sexual violence. In support of local efforts, programme support helped national and local stakeholders in implementing a national strategy to combat sexual and gender-based violence in Eastern Congo. The programme was comprised of five key components: fighting against impunity; protection and prevention; reforming the security sector; multi-sector assistance, and investments in data mapping, analysis, and dissemination.

JGE10.name: Joint Programme for Gender Equality in Georgia
JGE10.description: The UN Joint Programme for Gender Equality promotes gender equality and women’s empowerment in Georgia by strengthening the capacities of the Government at both the central and local levels across the executive, legislative and judicial branches, engaging civil society, and raising public awareness about gender equality.

JGT30.name: JP GTM Integral Rural Development in Ixil
JGT30.description: The Ixil Joint Programme for Integral Rural Development in Guatemala supports coordinated and community-centered responses to poverty, local governance, resource and disaster risk management, and rural development outcomes for people living in the region of Ixil.

JLS00.name: JP Lesotho Humanitarian
JLS00.description: The humanitarian response joint programme in Lesotho encompassed a holistic package of humanitarian-development nexus interventions to address the consequences of climate change-related drought. Stakeholders implemented complementary activities to rapidly and effectively respond to humanitarian needs in the areas of food security, agriculture, WASH, social protection, and coordination. By following a rights-based approach, initiatives were contextually sensitive to the rights and needs of affected populations while also covering multiple aspects of drought impact.

JMW00.name: JP Malawi Girls' Education
JMW00.description: The first phase of a joint programme on education for girls in Malawi, the Malawi Girls’ Education Joint Programme (JPGE) reduced poverty in targeted districts by providing quality education and life skills for adolescent girls. An inclusive, intersectional approach was used to address the issues that affecting girls’ access to education and ability to stay in school.

JMZ00.name: Action for Girls and Young Women in Mozambique
JMZ00.description: The Action for Girls and Young Women's Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights in Mozambique Joint Programme applies behavioural and social change practices to shift attitudes that negatively affect young women. Approaches enable stakeholders to remove existing barriers that prevent young women from accessing the sexual and reproductive health rights (SRHR) services they want and need.

JXD00.name: JP Gender Nat Resources Peace
JXD00.description: As primary providers of basic needs in households and communities, women living in rural settings tend to be dependent on natural resources to sustain their families and earn an income. This makes them particularly vulnerable to changes in the availability and quality of resources during and after conflict with implications on community welfare in peacebuilding settings, where up to 40% of households are headed by women. To unlock this peacebuilding potential, stakeholders operating under the Gender-Responsive Approaches to Natural Resource Management for Peacebuilding Joint Programme closed gaps in the humanitarian-development nexus, coming up with novel solutions to address the natural resource issues women may have faced in post-conflict settings.

MDA00.name: Moldova Toward Unity in Action
MDA00.description: The Towards Unity in Action fund is an expression of the collective determination in Moldova to address national development challenges and meet international human rights commitments. Greater unity across stakeholders helps to accelerate progress on a variety of issues that include democratic governance, justice, equality and human rights. As such, stakeholders are able to leverage tools, approaches and reforms that create space for the establishment of efficient and sustainable administrative frameworks, improved institutional performance, and strengthened rule of law and human rights protection mechanisms. Cutting across all programme action is the promotion and protection of human rights, gender equality, and non-discrimination. Particular attention is paid to marginalized and vulnerable groups, and financing is articulated through context-specific thematic windows, making it possible for stakeholders to flexibly expand established projects and incorporate additional thematic windows according to levels of interest. Fund operations were extended until the end of December 2021 due to setbacks resulting from the COVID-19 pandemic.

RW100.name: Rwanda One UN Fund
RW100.description: The One UN pilot in Rwanda was launched to enable the delivery of more effective and coherent development responses that could meet the needs of the national government and its partners, as well as those central to every initiative: the people of Rwanda. In line with Delivering as One standard operating procedures, One UN Fund action was aligned with national and SDG targets, and a coherent approach was taken for responding to the humanitarian One UN agenda. Across the board, SDG policy gap analyses were undertaken to inform the government and other national stakeholders ways of incorporating SDG goals and targets into national and local strategies, polices and development plans.

SUN00.name: SUN Movement Fund
SUN00.description: To address the importance and urgency of under-nutrition around the world, stakeholders launched the Scaling Up Nutrition Movement (Sun Movement) at the 2012 United Nations Summit on the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs). Under this fund, stakeholders committed to action that would substantively scale up nutrition in 26 countries. The initiative was an unprecedented development in the field of nutrition, bringing together over 100 partners to coordinate and aligne global, national, and local efforts—rallying behind priority areas that could result in sustainable solutions for under-nutrition.

TZ100.name: Tanzania One UN Fund
TZ100.description: Through the Tanzania One UN Fund, established in 2007, the United Nations has mobilized and allocated over $265 million US dollars towards the achievement of national development priorities. The Fund currently supports the delivery of shared results anchored in the United Nations Development Assistance Plan (UNDAP II) 2016-2021, a critical instrument for responding to national needs and priorities, and in support of national efforts to achieve the 2030 Agenda.

VNM00.name: UN REDD Viet Nam Phase II MPTF
VNM00.description: Phase II of the UN REDD+ Viet Nam Programme carried forward efforts of Phase I in reducing emissions from deforestation and forest degradation across the South Asian country. Coinciding with the second of three reducing emissions from deforestation and forest degradation (REDD+) phases, the objective was to enhance the national government's ability to benefit from results-based payments for REDD+ and spur transformational changes in the forestry sector.

YEM00.name: Yemen National Dialogue and Constitutional Reform Trust Fund

3CD00.name: DRC Fonds National REDD MPTF
3CD00.description: Since 2010, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) National REDD+ Fund has supported the national government in the design and implementation of strategic and holistic low emission development projects that address deforestation and environmental degradation concerns across the country.

3ML00.name: Mali Climate Fund
3ML00.description: The Mali Climate Fund supports integrated and ambitious solutions—in line with the national strategy for disaster risk reduction and management—that mitigate the impact of climate change, improve biodiversity, reduce poverty, and achieve a resilient, green climate economy for all.

4CO00.name: Trust Fund for Peace in Colombia
4CO00.description: The United Nations Multi-Partner Trust Fund for Sustaining Peace in Colombia finances coordinated responses that guarantee stabilization through the design and implementation of people and peace-centered agreements, frameworks, and programmes.

4SO00.name: Somalia Joint Fund
4SO00.description: The Somalia Joint Fund accelerates the UN’s contribution to sustainable and peaceful development in Somalia by providing a platform for joint policy and strategic dialogue that translates into high-quality and flexible programming across seven priority areas.

BT100.name: Bhutan UN Country Fund
BT100.description: The UN Bhutan Country Fund (One Fund) mobilized resources for United Nations activities at the country level. It served as an instrument for partners to pool and allocate financing that spurred progress toward achieving Bhutan One Programme (2014-2018) outcomes.

CCF00.name: UN-REDD Programme Fund
CCF00.description: The UN-REDD Programme Fund supports nationally-led REDD+ processes that promote the informed and meaningful involvement of all stakeholders—with a focus on indigenous people and communities dependent on forests—in implementing national and international REDD+ priorities and commitments. ​

HCF10.name: Central African Republic Humanitarian Fund
HCF10.description: The Central African Republic (CAR) Humanitarian Fund is a pooled mechanism that relies on coordinated efforts to deliver humanitarian assistance across the country. Allocations support projects that prioritize one or more of the Coordinated Aid Programme strategic priorities, and partners embrace a rights-based approach in providing humanitarian, emergency, and recovery assistance. For full information on results and resources: UN OCHA CAR and the CBPF Data Hub.

HRF00.name: UNDG Haiti Reconstruction Fund
HRF00.description: The United Nations Development Group (UNDG) Haiti Reconstruction Fund supports the Government of Haiti by financing recovery, reconstruction, and development projects that address social, economic, and environmental challenges caused by the January 2010 earthquake. The Fund provides flexible resources for development partners to accelerate short-term impact and progress towards SDG achievement.

HSO10.name: Somalia Humanitarian Fund
HSO10.description: Since 2011, the Somalia Humanitarian Fund has financed life-saving humanitarian aid and support to Somalia’s most vulnerable people. With a focus on the underserved and hard-to access areas, the Fund has strengthened the leadership, coordination and efficacy of responses to environmental shocks and prolonged armed conflict. Flexible and efficient, the Fund collaborates with local partners and other stakeholders to improve food, water, and personal security, as well as access to basic services. For full information on results and resources: UN OCHA Somalia and the CBPF Data Hub.

JBD40.name: Bangladesh Local Government Initiative on Climate Change
JBD40.description: Established in 2016, the Joint Programme Local Government Initiative on Climate Change (LoGIC) in Bangladesh promotes local action on climate change adaptation. Programme stakeholders seek to enhance the capacity of vulnerable communities, local government institutions, and civil society organizations around planning and financing climate change adaptation solutions in climate vulnerable areas.

JBY00.name: JP Belarus BELMED
JBY00.description: The Joint Programme Preventing Non-communicable Diseases, Promoting Healthy Lifestyles and Support to the Modernization of the Health System in Belarus supports activities that improve the national health system and welfare of Belarusian people.

JGT00.name: JP Guatemala Maya Programme
JGT00.description: The Maya Joint Programme in Guatemala contributes to improving the situation of the Maya, Xinca, and Garifuna people by advocating for an equal and fair justice system, supporting their right to bilingual and intercultural education, and autonomous political rights and representation.

JLA10.name: JP Lao Strengthening Capacity and Service Delivery of Local Administrations

JSO00.name: JP Somalia Loc Gov & Decentral
JSO00.description: This joint venture was established to support stakeholders in improving effective and efficient management outcomes in regional and district councils, which helped to increase public investment in basic services and strengthen civic participation in local decision-making processes for sustainable development.

JUG00.name: JP for AIDS Support in Uganda
JUG00.description: The Joint United Nations Programme of Support on AIDS in Uganda compliments the national HIV response by collaborating closely with national and local partners to reduce new HIV infections, secure sustainable financing for treatment, and attain 90-90-90 targets.

LBY00.name: Libya Recovery Trust Fund
LBY00.description: The Libya Recovery Trust Fund was anchored by United Nations Security Council Resolutions 1970, 1973, and 2009. Coherent with the principles of national ownership and rapid delivery, Fund stakeholders focused on the effective coordination and delivery of international assistance.

SDG00.name: Sustainable Development Goals Fund
SDG00.description: The Sustainable Development Goals Fund (SDG-F) was a multi-donor and multi-agency development cooperation mechanism created in 2014 to support sustainable development activities through integrated and multi-dimensional joint programmes. Stakeholders built on the experience, knowledge, lessons learned, and best practices of the Millennium Development Goals while expanding action to encompass sustainable development and the importance of public-private partnerships. The SDG-F operated at the country level through joint programmes implemented by the United Nations in collaboration with national counterparts and relevant stakeholders. Joint actions were localized and aligned with national priorities and SDG principles. Gender and women’s empowerment was a cross-cutting priority in all areas.

WAV00.name: UN Trust Fund to End VAW
WAV00.description: The United Nations Trust Fund in to End Violence against Women was a leading multilateral financial mechanism exclusively devoted to supporting local efforts to end violence against women and girls. Administered by UN Women on behalf of the United Nations development system, fund operations drew from the technical expertise and collaborative action of dozens of stakeholders and partners. With a focus on advancing the policy and plan implementation, UN Trust Fund stakeholders invested in initiatives that translated promises and recommendations into action and, ultimately, deliverables with tangible results. Concrete benefits were not only achieved for survivors of violence, but also contributed to the prevention of violence via $86 million US dollars for 351 initiatives in 128 countries and territories.

APF00.name: Counter-Piracy Trust Fund
APF00.description: Established in 2012 as a response to Security Council resolution S/RES/1851, Counter-Piracy Trust Fund stakeholders coordinate international efforts in fighting piracy off the coast of Somalia—an action that adversely affects the delivery of humanitarian aid, commercial shipping routes, and regional trade in the Horn of Africa. Coordinated action is essential to defray costs associated with prosecuting suspected pirates and implementing stakeholder objectives to combat piracy in all its forms.

CV100.name: Cabo Verde 2030 Acceleration Fund
CV100.description: The Cape Verde Transition Fund supports the coherent resource mobilization, allocation and disbursement of new donor resources to unfunded elements of the country’s One Programme and to new initiatives responding to emerging needs within the context of the One UN Programme and the ‘‘Delivering as One’’. Through the joint work of UN agencies in Cape Verde, the Transition Fund enables communities and people to see improvements to their lives and the services they receive.

EBO00.name: Ebola Response MPTF
EBO00.description: A wake-up call to strengthen the accessibility, resiliency and quality of health care systems and measures for everyone, everywhere, the 2014 Ebola epidemic tore through communities in Guinea, Sierra Leone, Liberia and parts of the Democratic Republic of Congo. A precursor to subsequent epidemics and pandemics, it showed what can happen when governments and health care staff are not prepared, shedding light on healthcare, sociopolitical, and cultural gaps that must be closed to cope with health emergencies...then and now In response to the Ebola crisis, the United Nations mobilized stakeholders to attain the highest level of donor engagement ever seen in a United Nations trust fund. Financing helped strengthen readiness responses to prevent the spread of Ebola and improve recovery measures in countries that bore the brunt of the crisis. Projects built and scaled up health care capacities and infrastructure in multiple sectors and succeeded in engaging and assisting the hardest hit communities.

ET100.name: Ethiopia One UN Fund
ET100.description: The Ethiopia One UN Fund was established in 2011 as a funding mechanism for new resources pooled by donors to support underfunded portions of the One UN Programme, including gender empowerment, maternal health, and equitable development. The Fund seeks to strengthen the planning and coordination progress, align funding allocations to the needs of the UNDAF, and channel funds towards the highest priority needs of the country.

GAI00.name: Women’s Peace and Humanitarian Fund
GAI00.description: The Women’s Peace and Humanitarian Fund provides flexible and fast financing for integrated interventions that increase women’s participation in response to crises and emergencies, as well as preventing conflict, encouraging national ownership of development investments, and upholding peacebuilding commitments. For more information on how to contribute, contact the Head of the Secretariat. Your contribution will support quality interventions that enhance the capacities of women civil society leaders and local organizations to prevent conflict, respond to emergencies, and seize key peacebuilding opportunities in conflict and crises contexts around the world.

HCG10.name: DRC Humanitarian Fund
HCG10.description: The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) Humanitarian Fund applies coordinated approaches in delivering humanitarian assistance across the country. Advancing aid reforms through strategic programming and expanding networks, the Fund supports projects that fall under multiple emergency, recovery, and sustainable development clusters. Donate For full information on results and resources: UN OCHA DRC and the CBPF Data Hub.

HRM00.name: Human Rights Mainstreaming Fund
HRM00.description: The Human Rights Mainstreaming Multi-Donor Trust Fund (HRM Fund) supports UN Development System (UNDS) efforts to respond to the call by Member States for UNDS entities to assist countries in their efforts to respect and fulfill human rights obligations and commitments, including operationalizing the 2030 Agenda pledge to leave no one behind. Leveraging opportunities presented by the UNDS repositioning, the Fund enables the empowered, independent UN Resident Coordinators and new generation UN Country Teams to advance the values of the UN Charter and ensure that human rights are at the heart of implementing the 2030 Agenda through coherent, system-wide policies and coordinated inter-agency action at all levels.

HSD20.name: Sudan Humanitarian Fund
HSD20.description: The Sudan Humanitarian Fund (SHF) is a multi-donor country-based pooled fund managed by OCHA Sudan under the leadership of the Humanitarian Coordinator. It receives unearmarked contributions from donors – mainly governments – into a single fund. The funds are used for ongoing humanitarian operations and to respond to new emergencies. This is done through Standard Allocations and Reserve for Emergency Allocations. The SHF reinforces and relies on existing coordination structures, which allows for evidence-based prioritization and complementarity with humanitarian, development and peacebuilding funding mechanisms. A positioning paper is developed every year which highlights the strategic focus and guides allocations for that year. For full information on results and resources: UN OCHA Sudan and the CBPF Data Hub.

HSS10.name: South Sudan Humanitarian Fund
HSS10.description: Launched in 2012, the South Sudan Humanitarian Fund (SSHF) supports the timely allocation and disbursement of resources to the most vulnerable communities in South Sudan. In addressing critical humanitarian needs, the Fund strengthens stakeholder responses, endorses Good Humanitarian Donorship (GHD) principles, and provides the Humanitarian Coordinator with increased flexibility to allocate resources to rapid response and emergency projects. For full information on results and resources: UN OCHA South Sudan and the CBPF Data Hub.

IRQ00.name: Iraq UNDAF Trust Fund
IRQ00.description: Aligned with the Iraq Five-Year National Development Plan, the Iraq UNDAF Fund supported the implementation of holistic and coordinated responses that complimented national development priorities and United Nations Development Assistance Framework.

JBD10.name: JP Bangladesh UZGP
JBD10.description: The Upazila Governance Joint Programme (UZGP) strengthened Upazila Parishads (UZP) systems by building the capacities of local government, offering policy support and ensuring participatory citizen engagement for local development, effective service delivery, and attainment of the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs). Joint programme stakeholder support helped equip Upazila Parishad functionaries through initiatives that increased the performance of local authorities and also significantly improved community participation in the planning, budgeting, and implementation of development projects that addressed social issues, such as violence against women, women’s economic empowerment and civil engagement, and the expansion of information services.

JKS10.name: JP Kosovo DEED
JKS10.description: The objective of the Diaspora Engagement in Economic Development (DEED) Joint Programme was to enhance the contribution of the diaspora in reducing poverty in Kosovo in the short-term, and making gains towards sustainable and gender equitable local economic development in the long run. Stakeholders worked towards these aims by facilitating saving and investment amongst Kosovars living abroad and for remittance-receiving households in Kosovo.

JPK00.name: Community Resilience and Recovery Support to FATA Joint Programme
JPK00.description: The Community Resilience and Recovery Support programme in Pakistan provides support to internally displaced people (IDPs) returning to Federally Administered Tribal Areas (FATA). Stakeholders improve livelihoods and food security, provide better access to basic services and community infrastructure, strengthen social cohesion, and increase the capacity of the FATA Secretariat.

NGA00.name: Nigeria Safe Schools Initiative Multi-Donor Trust Fund

RPD00.name: Global Disability Fund
RPD00.description: The Global Disability Fund (GDF) is a global multi-partner fund that delivers coordinated and collective programmes and innovations, and shares capacity building and evidence to support disability inclusion in developing countries. GDF works in stable and emergency contexts to accelerate inclusive development, build climate resilience, and ensure inclusive humanitarian context and recovery.

UNA00.name: UN Action Multi-Partner Trust Fund
UNA00.description: The UN Action Against Sexual Violence in Conflict unites the work of the UN system with the goal of ending sexual violence during and after armed conflict. In 2009 UN Action established a Multi-Partner Trust Fund to mobilize funds to support the UN Action Secretariat and programmatic activities. The UN Action Multi-Partner Trust Fund seeks to streamline joint programming, strengthen governance and finical management systems, and standardize reporting to donors.

4CF00.name: Ezingo Fund for the Central African Republic
4CF00.description: The Central African Republic Multi-Partner Trust Fund (Ezingo) mobilizes strategic resources for integrated humanitarian responses to ongoing national and cross-border stabilization, recovery, and security challenges. Approaches are comprehensive and coherent, fusing humanitarian action with development finance mechanisms in a push to identify sustainable solutions to the current crisis.

AFI00.name: Central African Forest Initiative
AFI00.description: The Central African Forest Initiative and Trust Fund support investments and reforms to address forest loss and fight poverty in the high-forest cover countries of Central Africa.

DRF00.name: United Nations Fund Darfur
DRF00.description: The United Nations Fund for Recovery Reconstruction and Development in Darfur (United Nations Darfur Fund) effectively implements the Darfur Development Strategy and recommendations from the Doha Document for Peace in Darfur. The Fund supports Darfur’s transition from humanitarian assistance to recovery and development.

HAF10.name: Afghanistan Humanitarian Fund
HAF10.description: The Afghanistan Humanitarian Fund (AHF) Afghanistan is one of OCHA’s country-based pooled funds (CBPFs). It was established in 2014 for swift and strategic humanitarian action in Afghanistan. The AHF is under the authority of the Humanitarian Coordinator (HC), which gives the HC a greater ability to target available funds to the most critical humanitarian needs and enable efficient and rapid response to emergencies. For full information on results and resources: UN OCHA Afghanistan and the CBPF Data Hub.

IPP00.name: United Nations Indigenous Peoples’ Partnership
IPP00.description: With more than 370 million people around the world belonging to indigenous communities and indigenous knowledge was (and remains) crucial for linking development, human rights, peace, security, and environmental sustainability. Stakeholders involved in the United Nations Indigenous Peoples’ Partnership (UNIPP) sought to leverage the voices of indigenous people in Bolivia, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Congo, Nepal, and Nicaragua in support of strategic initiatives at local and national levels. The fund was the first global inter-agency initiative with a programmatic focus on indigenous people at the country level that was complemented by contextually-relevant interventions at regional and international levels.

JBA00.name: Joint Programme Seeking Care, Support and Justice for Survivors of Conflict Related Sexual Violence
JBA00.description: By providing the national government and civil society with new tools to comprehensively address the unresolved legacy of conflict related sexual violence (CRSV) that took place between 1992-1995 in Bosnia and Herzegovina, programme stakeholders helped design and launch services for all survivors through new transitional justice and survivor-centered approaches. Anchoring projects in justice, rule of law, and psychosocial care helped enhance the status of, and provide redress to, survivors through the development and expansion of reparations, rehabilitation, and equal access to services and justice. Efforts were also made to combat survivor stigmatization.

JBD20.name: JP Bangladesh Union Parishad
JBD20.description: Focusing on improving governance in the Union Parishads of Bangladesh was a way of establishing and supporting efficient institutions that could effectively contribute to deepening local democracies, energize local economies, and delivery quality, social services. The Union Parishad Governance Programme strengthened local government and stakeholder capacities to foster participatory local service delivery according to Millennium Development Goal (MDG) mandates.

JCG20.name: JP DRC Fighting Impunity
JCG20.description: Following a decade of conflict, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) initiated a slow transition towards restoring peace and security, particularly in the hard-hit eastern provinces. Sexual violence committed during bouts of conflict was amply documented with findings showing that rape was often used as a strategy of war. Furthermore, sexual and gender-based violence was a common occurrence with offences carried out by military members and civilians due to a climate of impunity that protected perpetrators.

JEG00.name: Social Economic and Legal Empowerment of Egyptian Women Joint Programme
JEG00.description: Women and girls in Egypt encounter multiple, intersectional challenges that affect their ability to fully participate in socio-economic life. The Egypt Women’s Empowerment Joint Programme addressed several inequality gaps and made contextually-relevant contributions to advance gender equality and the empowerment of women by targeting three pillars: social, legal, and economic empowerment. Aligned with the UNDAF for 2013–2017, the programme brought local and national stakeholders together to devise programmatic and policy solutions that would break ground for women to engage more in civil society as main agents of change. Programme stakeholders took action to find solutions for ongoing social, economic, and structural challenges and ways of increasing women’s equal participation in society based on citizenship rights.

JGH10.name: UN Programme on Ebola Virus Disease Preparedness in Ghana

JGT20.name: JP GTM Programme for Rural Development in Cuilco
JGT20.description: The Joint Programme for Integral Rural Development in the Upper Cuilco Basin of San Marcos supports coordinated and people-centered responses that improve resource and disaster risk management systems, and achieve rural development outcomes for communities of Guatemala’s Cuilco River high basin.

JKE20.name: JP Kenya Low Carb Climate Devt

JKH00.name: JP Cambodia Disability Rights
JKH00.description: The Cambodia Disability Rights Initiative Joint Programme was used by stakeholders to improve the quality of life for people living with disabilities in Cambodia. Although aspirational and challenging to achieve, stakeholders worked to create safe spaces for people living with disabilities and advocate for behavioural and structural changes that gave people with disabilities increased access to quality care and better opportunities to participate in social, economic, cultural and political life. All programmatic elements were designed to push the needle on SDG achievement—goals 4, 8, 10, and 3 in particular.

JKZ10.name: JP Kazakhstan Kyzylorda
JKZ10.description: Results-oriented and collaborative, the Kazakhstan Kyzylorda Joint Programme helped improve the well-being and quality of life for people living in Kyzylorda, a region heavily affected by environmental and developmental challenges. Innovative approaches implemented under the joint programme delivered economic, social, and solutions to affected local populations, particularly the most vulnerable.

JKZ20.name: JP Kazakhstan Mangystau
JKZ20.description: By placing engagement and intersectionality at the core of programme development and policymaking stakeholders of the Kazakhstan Mangystau Joint Programme were able to address socio-economic issues when modernizing the oil rich region of Mangystau, which has (in the past) been exposed to severe climatic conditions. Together with the Government of Kazakhstan, the United Nations Country Team collaborated on sustainable, socio-economic solutions that took into account climate change issues, ending violence against women and girls, improving access to quality sexual and reproductive health, spreading child care best practices, enhancing disaster risk reduction, improving data collection and analysis, and launching policies that would reverse growing social and regional disparities in rural areas.

JNE00.name: JP Niger Developpement Maradi
JNE00.description: In Niger, people living in the region of Maradi faced multiple, intersecting challenges that affected the quality of their lives. The Maradi Development Joint Programme was an opportunity for stakeholders to design and promote joint programs that improved the coherence and complementarity of collective responses in raising the resilience of local communities and institutions. Programme partners ensured their actions were aligned with national and local priorities to achieve a broader, significant impact throughout Maradi—especially for the most vulnerable.

JPS00.name: JP oPt Rule of Law
JPS00.description: To develop and maintain conditions for a viable State of Palestine based on international principles of rule of law and gender equality, programme stakeholders sought to improve the capacities of, and raise public confidence in, rule of law institutions. This was done by strengthening access to justice, security and protection services—especially for women and girls Sustainability designed, programme outcomes were aligned with system-level policy development measures. By combining enhanced service delivery that render justice and security institutions more resilient it played a role in improving public access to said services and hold duty-bearers to account. Support was catalytic in strengthening state-society relationships and establishing an enabling environment for medium-term development.

JXB00.name: Pacific Financial Inclusion Joint Programme
JXB00.description: The Pacific Financial Inclusion Joint Programme responds to current and emerging challenges in the finance sector by playing a critical role in expanding inclusive financial services for rural and low-income women, men, youth, and micro-entrepreneurs. Results are achieved through performance-based grants for financial service providers, market research, and technical assistance.

JYE00.name: Joint Programme Enhanced Rural Resilience in Yemen
JYE00.description: Launched in four governorates across Yemen, the Enhanced Rural Resilience Joint Programme for Yemen helped to increase the resilience and self-reliance of crisis-affected rural communities through the provision of support in the areas of livelihood stabilization, local governance and improved access to sustainable energy. By focusing on areas where gaps were prevalent, stakeholders could better engage communities and follow their lead in managing local risks and shocks for increased economic self-reliance and enhanced social cohesion. A secondary—but equally important—outcome of the joint programme approach led to improved institutional development and the curation of systems that are more responsive, accountable and effective in delivering services or meeting community-identified needs.

JZM00.name: JP Zambia Gender Based Violence
JZM00.description: The Joint Programme on gender-based violence (GBV) was developed to support the Government of the Republic of Zambia in implementing the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination Against Women (CEDAW), with particular focus on recommendations to bring about an end to violence against women and adopting ways of facilitating institutional transformation in the implementation of the Zambia Anti-GBV Act.

LRF00.name: Lebanon Recovery Fund
LRF00.description: The Lebanon Recovery Fund is a flexible pooled funding mechanism for channeling international assistance to the Government of Lebanon in support of national recovery and reconstruction efforts. Since 2017, the Recovery Fund has shifted its focus to support the implementation 2030 Agenda through joint programme initiatives that fall under the United Nations Strategic Framework for 2017-2020.

ME100.name: Montenegro UN Country Fund
ME100.description: The Delivering as One modality was vital for stakeholders in Montenegro to launch transformative development initiatives. Strategic priorities of the Montenegro UN Country Fund were streamlined through four results areas, each building on the experience of the UN in-country and collaborative efforts of partners in the realms of democratic governance, environmental sustainability, social inclusion, and economic governance. All programme initiatives had human rights, gender equality, national capacity development components mainstreamed throughout and, aligned with national priorities, programme interventions were adapted (where possible) to meet relevant SDG indicators and make progress toward 2030 Agenda achievement.

MW100.name: Malawi One UN Fund
MW100.description: The One UN Fund in Malawi was launched in early 2006 to stress the importance of the United Nations reform in making national and global development systems more efficient and effective when delivering joint results. Under the ‘Delivering as One’ umbrella, stakeholders in Malawi worked to progressively implement the framework and align responses with national strategies. Collective action on United Nations reform processes, procedures, and frameworks enabled stakeholders to accelerate national and local SDG targets and cover ground toward 2030 Agenda achievement. As a follow up, the UN in Malawi established the Malawi SDG Acceleration Fund in 2018.

MZ100.name: Mozambique One UN Fund
MZ100.description: The presence of a unified United Nations that plans, acts, and delivers as one in Mozambique has proved essential for the delivery of concrete development and humanitarian results that support national development objectives and priorities. Inspired by Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) ambitions and global commitments, the Mozambique One UN Fund offers a shared approach to the design and implementation of innovative responses and programmes. Fund stakeholders focus on collaborating with government, private sector, academia, local organizations, and communities to put forward contextually shaped solutions that are aligned with national plans and SDG principles.

PB000.name: Peacebuilding Fund
PB000.description: The UN Secretary-General’s Peacebuilding Fund is the organization's financial instrument of first resort to sustain peace in countries or situations at risk or affected by violent conflict. The Fund invests with UN entities, governments, regional organizations, multilateral banks, national multi-donor trust funds or civil society organizations. The Fund works across pillars and supports integrated UN responses to fill critical gaps; respond quickly and with flexibility to peacebuilding opportunities; and catalyze processes and resources in a risk-tolerant fashion.

PG100.name: Papua New Guinea UN Country Fund
PG100.description: The Papua New Guinea United Nations Country Fund supports national priorities through the strategic implementation of the United Nations Development Assistance Framework (UNDAF) that cover primary components of the Sustainable Development Goals. Central to the Fund are joint planning, implementation, and reporting to minimize duplication of efforts, improve resource allocation, and centralize data collection and analysis on the road to 2030 Agenda achievement.

PK100.name: Pakistan One Fund
PK100.description: One Fund stakeholders embraced Sustainable Development Goal (SDGs) targets and sought to implement the most ambitious national development framework to date: Vision 2025. The Pakistan One Fund was used as a vehicle for the United Nations, government, and national partners to collectively work towards fostering social justice, strengthening national capacities and addressing inequalities by way of integrated humanitarian and development action. With a focus on six priority areas, ownership of development progress was eventually handed over to national changemakers and people living in Pakistan, especially the most vulnerable and marginalized. By aligning projects with national plans and taking into account United Nations reform processes and international frameworks stakeholders were able to accelerate contextually-relevant development and humanitarian outcomes, and accelerate SDG achievement.

RWF00.name: Economic Empowerment of Rural Women
RWF00.description: A global initiative, the Economic Empowerment of Rural Women MPTF aims to accelerate progress towards securing the livelihoods, rights and resilience of rural women by building on the comparative advantages of partners to improve socioeconomic opportunities for women in rural areas. Initiatives help rural women enhance food security status, leadership opportunities, community participation, access to social protection, legal, and economic services, and boosting their productive potential.

VN100.name: Viet Nam One Plan Fund I

VN200.name: Viet Nam One Plan Fund II
VN200.description: The Viet Nam One Plan Fund II was a pooled mechanism for mobilizing and allocating resources in support of unfunded portions of the plan and new initiatives designed to respond to emerging needs. Areas of action under the Fund included job opportunities and livelihood security, multi-dimensional poverty, gender inequality, shrinking civil society spaces, and climate-related hazards. Building on stakeholder achievements under the previous One Plan Fund, phase II was meant to realize SDG-related outcomes by strengthening planning and coordination processes, mobilizing allocations for the One Plan II, and channeling funding towards the highest priority needs. One Plan II programmes were innovative, integrated, supportive and complimentary to those launched by the Government of Viet Nam when transitioning toward programming for Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and 2030 Agenda outcomes.

BW100.name: Botswana UN Country Fund
BW100.description: The Botswana UN Country Fund facilitated government and United Nations programme operational plan outcomes by channeling consistent and predictable financing to priority areas through a pooled investments.

CDS00.name: DRC Stabilization Coherence Fund
CDS00.description: Created in 2016, the DRC Stabilization Coherence Fund is the principal programmatic mechanism for project implementation under the International Security and Stabilization Support Strategy (ISSSS). Finances are invested in six projects in six priority zones of the Democratic Republic of Congo, in support of Fund management, monitoring and evaluation practices, and political engagement.

KEN00.name: SDG Multi-Partner Trust Fund Kenya
KEN00.description: The Kenya SDG Partnership Platform Multi-Partner Trust Fund builds on past success to attain the SDGs by 2030. In supporting key catalytic interventions within the Kenya UNSDCF, partners translate effective and transparent cooperation into inclusive outcomes that maximize investments and accelerate sustainable development.

MCS00.name: Migration Compact Support MPTF
MCS00.description: The Start-Up Fund for Safe, Orderly, and Regular Migration Multi-Partner Trust Fund supports the adoption and implementation of the Global Compact, encouraging the uptake of migration approaches that benefit communities of origin, transit, and destination, as well as migrants themselves.

PGE00.name: Partnership for Action on Green Economy
PGE00.description: The Partnership for Action on Green Economy (PAGE) puts sustainability and social equity at the heart of global economic policymaking. Reframing existing practices around sustainability not only fosters economic growth, but also increases incomes, creates jobs, reduces poverty and inequality, and strengthens the ecological foundations of national economies.

JCG40.name: JP DRC ACTIF
JCG40.description: The Action, Change, and Transformation Through Inclusive Finance (ACTIF) in DRC programme promotes inclusion and socio-economic equality—connecting people living in remote rural areas with contemporary financial tools and services. Programme activities strengthen the country’s financial sector and contribute to the achievement of several Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the National Roadmap for Financial Inclusion.

3ET00.name: Ethiopia Climate Resilient Green Economy Facility
3ET00.description: The Ethiopia Climate Resilient Green Economy (CRGE) Facility pursues economic growth, net-zero emissions, and building resilience amongst local communities by positioning Ethiopia at the forefront of the low carbon revolution. Unlocking potential in the national forestry and renewable resource sectors, the Facility helps stakeholders achieve inclusive, lucrative, and strategic Green Economy outcomes.

GLR00.name: Great Lakes Region Cross-Border Fund
GLR00.description: The Great Lakes Region (GLR) Cross-Border Fund is a pooled funding mechanism that tackles cross-border aspects of peace and security. Its activities lead to improved trust and community building in affected areas, and facilitates improved coherence and coordination among United Nations organizations in the Great Lakes Region of Africa.

IPS00.name: Joint SDG Fund
IPS00.description: Joint SDG Fund is an inter-agency mechanism that incentivizes transformative policy and financing to shift and stimulate strategic investments required to catalyze and accelerate progress against the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) at the country level. The flexibility and demand-based approach Fund stakeholders are afforded caters to the specific needs of diverse UN country teams and has been critical in effectively responding to the COVID-19 pandemic and stimulating SDG integration in national systems and programmes.

JLK00.name: JP Sri Lanka Catalytic PB
JLK00.description: The EU Catalytic Support to Peacebuilding Programme (EU-CSBP) supports the Government of Sri Lanka’s efforts to consolidate and sustain peace and democracy gains by providing technical assistance to achieve the priorities identified in the Peacebuilding Priority Plan, which include transitional justice, reconciliation, good governance and resettlement, and durable solutions.

JMW10.name: JP Malawi Girls' Education II
JMW10.description: Following the success of the first phase of the joint programme on education for girls in Malawi, the Malawi Girls’ Education Joint Programme (JPGE) II continues to reduce poverty in three districts by providing quality education and basic life skills for adolescent girls. A cross-sector approach is used to address various issues affecting girls’ access to education and their ability to stay in school.

SDN00.name: Sudan Rule of Law and HR
SDN00.description: The Joint Programme for Rule of Law and Human Rights in Darfur strengthens the delivery and coherence of United Nations support, bringing together relevant programmes under one framework. Fund resources are allocated to initiatives that tackle lawlessness and criminality—two of the primary causes of instability in Darfur today.

JMG00.name: Joint Programme to Support to the Androy Region in Madagascar

SIF00.name: Spotlight Initiative Fund
SIF00.description: Spotlight Initiative, a collaborative venture by the United Nations and European Union, invests in programmes that improve the rights and opportunities of women and girls around the world through the prevention of and response to all forms of violence against women and girls. Pointing the light toward the shadows, Spotlight supports comprehensive and inclusive approaches that enable women and girls to live lives free from the debilitating experience or effects of harmful practices and various forms of violence.

4X100.name: JP Syria Urban and Rural Resilience
4X100.description: The United Nations Joint Programme to Build Urban and Rural Resilience and the Conditions for Recovery in Syria creates an opening for stakeholders to respond to the needs of people and their communities through recovery and resilience efforts in the areas of basic social service provision, improved livelihoods, social cohesion, and addressing local causes of conflict.

ETH00.name: Ethiopia New Way Platform
ETH00.description: The Support to Livelihoods of Drought Affected Households and Resilience Building of Vulnerable Groups in Warder and Kebredahar Woredas of Ethiopia’s Somali Region is a joint programme that seeks to stabilize the livelihoods of those threatened by drought and strengthen the resilience of pastoral and agro-pastoral communities to reduce the impact of droughts and climate risks.

JGE30.name: Joint Programme on Improving Vocational Education in Abkhazia
JGE30.description: The European Union and United Nations-supported joint programme on improving vocational education in Abkhazia, Georgia, increases the quality, effectiveness and accessibility of vocational education and training (VET) for people to address their actual needs and building skills and capacities that improve employability and self-employment irrespective of one's nationality or place of residence.

JPS10.name: Promoting Rule of Law in Palestine (Sawasya II)
JPS10.description: Sawasya II (Promoting Rule of Law in Palestine) is a joint programme that advances human rights, rule of law, gender justice, and access to justice across the State of Palestine, with a strong focus on women and children. Its integrated programmatic framework contributes to priority areas in line with 2030 Agenda and Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) targets as well as to the National Policy Agenda for the State of Palestine.

JWS00.name: Women in Leadership in Samoa
JWS00.description: The Women in Leadership in Samoa Joint Programme supports stakeholders in addressing challenges to women’s representation and civic engagement. Activities enhance all women’s leadership to take sustainable action in their communities. Initiatives also support women candidates planning to run in the 2021 elections, as well as Members of Parliament in operationalizing the SDGs and 2030 Agenda.

LNS00.name: The Lion's Share Fund
LNS00.description: A multi-partner platform for private sector corporations, philanthropists, foundations, and global/local non-governmental organizations, the Lion’s Share Fund tackles current wildlife conservation and animal welfare crises by redirecting advertising funds to augment biodiversity and sustainable animal-care practices.

JBD50.name: JP Bangladesh SAFE
JBD50.description: The UN Joint Programme Safe Access to Cooking Fuel and Energy (JP Bangladesh SAFE) provides food security, nutrition and energy solutions to 125,000 refugee and host community households in the Cox’s Bazar district of Bangladesh, where the majority of Rohingya refugees sought refute after fleeing Myanmar in 2017. Nearly a million people, refugees and host communities, that reside in the area require humanitarian assistance.

JCG50.name: JP DRC Fight Against GBV - JAD
JCG50.description: The Joint Programme, Fight Against Gender Based Violence: Justice, Empowerment, and Dignity for Women and Girls in the Democratic Republic of Congo, contributes to the reduction of GBV by shifting socio-cultural attitudes and norms in favour of gender equal systems and services. Initiatives are designed to further empower women and girls, and raise the resilience of survivors of gender-based violence.

LTF00.name: Law and Order Trust Fund for Afghanistan
LTF00.description: The Law and Order Trust Fund for Afghanistan (LOTFA) mobilizes strategic resources in support of development strategies that strengthen national justice and rule of law systems. Initiatives close existing gaps in the security and justice sectors of Afghanistan with a strong focus on anti-corruption.

PK200.name: UN Sustainable Development Framework Fund for Pakistan
PK200.description: The UN Sustainable Development Framework (UNSDF) Fund for Pakistan supports investments that accelerate the SDGs and lead to transformative humanitarian and development changes across the country. By investing in historically underfunded areas and innovative joint programmes, the Fund strengthens national capacities, grows partnerships, improves data collection and analysis, and helps stakeholders address bottlenecks that threaten to block SDG progress.

RDS00.name: United Nations Road Safety Trust Fund
RDS00.description: Established in 2018, the United Nations Road Safety Fund (UNRSF) aims to sustainably improving road safety worldwide and to support countries in achieving road safety-related Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Fund stakeholders explore innovative mechanisms to raise contributions from private sector companies, as well as UN member state countries.

RW200.name: Rwanda SDG Fund
RW200.description: The Rwanda Sustainable Development Fund 2018 to 2023 mobilizes and allocates additional resources to activities under the United Nations Development Assistance Plan (UNDAP II), which supports the national sustainable development agenda of Rwanda. The Fund strengthens planning and coordination process, provides investments for SDG acceleration, improves coherence, reduces fragmentation and transaction costs, and promotes the uptake of innovative modes of financing.

WHL00.name: Working for Health Multi-Partner Trust Fund
WHL00.description: A strategic, multi-stakeholder pooled fund, the Working for Health MPTF helps realize a world where everyone has equal access to health services. It supports United Nations Member States and stakeholders in the creation of 40 million new health jobs (needed by 2030) and adopting methods of averting the shortfall of health-workers, primarily in low- and lower-middle income countries.

FSA00.name: Multi-Partner Trust Fund Building a Strategy for Financing the 2030 Agenda
FSA00.description: Strategic financing—critical for realizing the Sustainable Development Goals—is central to the Building a Strategy for Financing the 2030 Agenda Multi-Partner Trust Fund. Looking to earlier models and approaches, the Trust Fund helps partners overcome ongoing structural and systematic weaknesses to make economic and policy progress towards achieving the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and Paris Agreement on Climate Change

JMZ10.name: Action for Girls and Young Women (Rapariga Biz)
JMZ10.description: The Joint Programme Action for Girls and Young Women (Rapariga Biz) in Mozambigue applies behavioural and social change practices to shift attitudes that negatively affect young women. Approaches enable stakeholders to remove existing barriers that prevent young women from accessing the sexual and reproductive health rights (SRHR) services they want and need.

SSR00.name: South Sudan RSRTF
SSR00.description: The South Sudan Reconciliation, Stabilization, and Resilience Trust Fund (South Sudan RSRTF) pioneers an innovative whole-of-system approach in implementing reconciliation, stabilization, and resilience components that, together, build peace and stability. Stakeholders of this interagency pooled fund support South Sudan communities in realizing the economic and livelihood outcomes of sustained peace and benefits of accelerating SDG and 2030 Agenda outcomes.

4LG00.name: Liptako-Gourma Regional JP
4LG00.description: Launched by the UNDP sub-regional hub in Dakar, Joint Programme stakeholders support Liptako-Gourma regional authorities in effectively strengthening human development action in cross border areas of Burkina Faso, Mali, and Niger. In establishing an enabling environment through improved planning, management, and coordination, stakeholders improve aid effectiveness responses, offer innovative approaches for crisis prevention, and also raise resilience, opportunities for job creation, and revitalize the economies of local communities.

4LR00.name: Liberia Multi-Partner Trust Fund
4LR00.description: The Liberia Multi-Partner Trust Fund (LMPTF), launched in 2019, helps development stakeholders holistically embed Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) approaches and targets into national plans and policies. In doing so, the government ensures continued progress in consolidating peace, embracing inclusive development practices, and creating locally owned programmes and processes.

AMR00.name: Antimicrobial Resistance Multi-Partner Trust Fund
AMR00.description: The Antimicrobial Resistance Multi-Partner Trust Fund (MPTF) combats the threat of antimicrobial drug resistance through strategic collaboration, sustainable streams of capital, and Sustainable Development Goal-focused responses that support localized ‘One Health’ National Action Plans.

JMM00.name: Women’s Empowerment and Inclusive Communities in Myanmar
JMM00.description: Based on a 2018 joint project for inclusive development, the Women's Empowerment and Resilient Communities Joint Programme promotes gender equality and women’s empowerment in a bid to improve access to justice mechanisms, service delivery, inclusive development, and build community resilience in Rakhine State, Myanmar. Working closely with state officials, CSO leaders, and community members, joint programme stakeholders have localized and mainstreamed the SDGs into projects and advocacy efforts.

JMZ20.name: Mozambique Rapariga Biz
JMZ20.description: The scaled up version of the Joint Programme Mozambique Rapariga Biz (funded by the Government of Canada) addresses existing health disparities among adolescents in Mozambique by implementing initiatives that assist girls and young women to make informed decisions about their sexual and reproductive health and rights.

LKP00.name: UN Sri Lanka SDG Multi-Partner Trust Fund
LKP00.description: The UN Sri Lanka SDG multi-partner pooled (UNSLSDG) fund instrument will support an ambitious agenda for working together to unlock progress towards the 2030 Agenda and the SDGs. The Fund will have several thematic windows that will open gradually. For this phase, three windows on Peace, Resilience and National Planning and Finance will be opened.

MD100.name: Moldova 2030 SDGs Partnership
MD100.description: The Moldova SDG Partnership Fund supports the United Nations Country Team in mobilizing resources and expanding partner networks in a bid to accelerate SDG and 2030 Agenda progress. Fast-tracked programmes are designed to prompt change across five critical areas: governance, human rights, and gender equality; sustainable, inclusive, and equitable economic growth; environmental sustainability and resilience; inclusive and equitable social development, and COVID-19 pandemic management and responses.

ARL00.name: Aral Sea UN Human Security Trust Fund for the Aral Sea in Uzbekistan
ARL00.description: The Multi-Partner Human Security Trust Fund for the Aral Sea Region in Uzbekistan (MPHSTF) uses a multi-sector and people-centered approach to build the resilience of communities affected by the current ecological disaster. Responses are the result of unified programmatic approaches and the application of timely and coordinated environmental, economic, food, health, and social solutions.

CSV00.name: Conflict-Related Sexual Violence MPTF
CSV00.description: The Conflict-Related Sexual Violence Prevention Multi-Partner Trust Fund (CRSV-MPTF) enhances stakeholder accountability and response efforts towards preventing sexual violence in conflict settings by bringing attention to existing gaps and under-financed areas.

JBA10.name: Joint Programme Bosnia and Herzegovina DRR
JBA10.description: The Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) for Sustainable Development in Bosnia and Herzegovina Joint Programme supports local governments in improving institutional frameworks, public services and partnerships, and the capacities of the general population to be less vulnerable socially and economically in the face of disasters and climate change.

JGE20.name: Georgia-EU Innovative Action for Private Sector Competitiveness
JGE20.description: The Innovative Action for Private Sector Competitiveness Joint Programme in Georgia is a European Union-funded joint programme that enhances entrepreneurship and business sophistication by strengthening the capacities of the government and local entities to develop and operate clusters. It supports companies directly by providing strategic investments and connecting local businesses to diaspora groups for the purpose of knowledge and technology transfer and financing.

JYE10.name: JP Yemen ERRY II
JYE10.description: The Supporting Resilient Livelihoods and Food Security in Yemen Joint Programme (ERRY II) funds integrated initiatives that strengthen the resilience of crisis-affected communities in Yemen. Interventions are designed to reach the most vulnerable community members (e.g. women, the unemployed, youth, and internally displaced people) through the application of sustainable livelihood and basic service approaches.

JZM10.name: Joint Programme on Gender-Based Violence Zambia
JZM10.description: Building on the success of its first phase, the Government of the Republic of Zambia and United Nations, the Joint Programme on Gender Based Violence Phase II accelerates the implementation of health, protection, legal, and coordination programmes that enhance GBV prevention and responses at sub-national and national levels.

VN300.name: Viet Nam SDG Fund
VN300.description: The UN Viet Nam SDG Fund supports the integrated and coherent financing of the joint implementation of the One Strategic Plan for 2017 to 2021 in Viet Nam. This country-level pooled financing mechanism supports SDG acceleration and achievement of the 2030 Agenda by circumventing policy bottlenecks and unlocking SDG financing to mainstream human rights, gender and youth, and incorporate leave no one behind principles.

EIF00.name: Elsie Initiative Fund
EIF00.description: Established with the support of peacekeeping and governance experts, the Elsie Initiative Fund takes important steps in encouraging and funding innovation to accelerate the pace of change in security institutions and enable more uniformed women to deploy to, and meaningfully participate in, peace operations.

JPK10.name: Joint Programme for Quality Education in Pakistan
JPK10.description: The Improved Access to Quality Education in the Tribal Districts of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Joint Programme addresses the social and cultural barriers that prevent access to quality education for girls. Implemented under the One UN umbrella, partners align joint programme aims and outcomes with the current Education Sector Plan for Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

MW200.name: Malawi SDG Acceleration Fund
MW200.description: The Malawi SDG Acceleration Fund is a vehicle for development partners to pool resources in tackling strategic challenges for SDG achievement in Malawi. The Fund supports the coherent resource mobilization, allocation and disbursement of financing to under-funded and cross-sector areas where the United Nations has a comparative advantage in implementing sustainable solutions, together.

OPL00.name: One Planet Multi-Partner Trust Fund
OPL00.description: Fundamental changes in the way we consume and produce are imperative for protecting the planet. The One Planet Multi-Partner Trust Fund supports the necessary shift and offers incentives to national and global leaders to adopt adaptable solutions that overcome challenges to realizing SDG 12 and make good on the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.

4NP00.name: Nepal Devt. Framework MPTF
4NP00.description: Multiple natural hazards like earthquakes, floods, landslides and fires are a major source of risk in Nepal. Although disasters with the most severe humanitarian implications get addressed through emergency response preparedness plans closely aligned with government efforts, gaps remain. The United Nations, uniquely positioned in Nepal, assists stakeholders in reframing and expanding national and local disaster management protocols and systems, enhancing coordination, sharing information, ramping up data collection and analysis, and boosting humanitarian efforts vis-à-vis context sensitive disaster responses.

JCU00.name: JP Cuba EE FRE-DL
JCU00.description: Aligning national policy priorities with international compacts, the Local Development Support for Energy Efficient and Renewable Energy Sources in Cuba works by building on similar initiatives and implementing measures that improve energy efficiency across the country and support local development and uptake of renewable energy in rural communities.

MIG00.name: Migration Multi-Partner Trust Fund
MIG00.description: Committed to safe, orderly, and regular migration, the Migration Multi-Partner Trust Fund supports the adoption and implementation of the Global Compact to encourage the uptake of migration approaches that benefit communities of origin, transit, and destination, as well as migrants. Fund key documents Terms of Reference Joint Programmes Pipeline Operations Manual Latest Steering Committee decisions Investment Plan 2023-2026 Templates

SLW00.name: Western Balkans SALW Control Roadmap MPTF
SLW00.description: The Western Balkans Small Arms and Light Weapons (SALW) Control Roadmap Multi-Partner Trust Fund supports a donor-coordinated approach to the implementation of the Roadmap for a sustainable solution to the illegal possession, misuse and trafficking of SALW, their ammunition and explosives in the Western Balkans. This pooled fund strengthens coordination, planning and communication among all partners, fosters collaboration, strengthens results and reduces risks to governments and financial contributors through a comprehensive risk and results-based management system.

UTL00.name: UNITLIFE Trust Fund
UTL00.description: At the UNITLIFE Trust Fund, women are agents of change in addressing one of the world’s lesser known and underfunded diseases: chronic childhood malnutrition. UNITLIFE supports programmes that improve childhood malnutrition treatment availability and delivery, and expands women’s access to productive resources and livelihood opportunities.

JXF00.name: Joint Programme Financing a Green, Inclusive and Sustainable Recovery
JXF00.description: Building on the outcomes and progress made under the Financing Strategy 2030 Agenda Trust Fund Joint Programme, the Financing a Green, Inclusive and Sustainable Recovery Joint Programme aims to increase the scale and alignment of both public and private finance with the Sustainable Development Goals at the global, regional and country level with targeted support to vulnerable countries and regions including Small Island Developing States (SIDS), Least Developed Countries (LDCs), and the Sahel region, which continue to be disproportionately affected by the COVID-19 crisis.

UP100.name: UN Pacific Strategy Fund
UP100.description: The United Nations Pacific Strategy Fund enhances stakeholder coordination and coherence for financing and implementing programmes that address priorities laid out in the UN Pacific Strategy 2018 – 2022. Outcomes meet Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) targets while resources are directed to critical areas (e.g. climate change, gender equality, inclusive economic empowerment, etc.) and compliment the work of regional organizations.

JGE40.name: JP Georgia Human Rights for All Phase 2
JGE40.description: The Human Rights for All Joint Programme was established to raise human rights protections in Georgia, ensuring rights are compliant with national priorities, the constitution and major policy documents, as well as other international obligations like the European Union-Georgia Association Agreement, Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), and multiple UN human rights treaties. Stakeholders support the implementation and monitoring of national human rights policies and related frameworks, and collaborative action sets out to improve independent investigation instruments, evaluate measures designed to combat torture, advance personal data protection laws, and address challenges to human rights for everyone—focusing on minority groups, people from the LGBTQIA+ community, and those living with disabilities.

JIR00.name: Responding to emerging needs and enhancing the resilience of the most vulnerable, especially children, youth, and women in Iran JP
JIR00.description: The Emerging Needs Joint Programme in Iran boosts sustainable economic and social development in the areas of public health (children and youth focused), disaster risk reduction, and community resilience. Initiatives strengthen cancer treatment/medical resource supply chains for children, mainstream women’s empowerment and the needs of vulnerable populations in disaster preparedness responses, and enact comprehensive drug prevention and treatment services for youth. The programme supports network building for information sharing, enhancing government and community capacities, and accelerating 2030 Agenda progress multiple Sustainable Development Goals.

JLA20.name: JP Lao EVAW
JLA20.description: Stakeholders of Prevention and Elimination of Violence Against Women Joint Programme in Laos draw attention to the critical links between gender-based violence and achievement of the national development agenda, as well as the Sustainable Development Goals. Support to national authorities helps in the planning of integrated cross-sector initiatives that address and reduce GBV in the country.

JSO10.name: UN Joint Rule of Law Programme for Somaliland
JSO10.description: Stakeholders of this joint programme empower local communities to take part in the development and upholding of their rights related to security and justice. In doing so, individuals and collectives can set realistic goals and act in ways that result in locally owned gains that include measurable improvements to justice services for all that are guided by national standards and international norms, and hold sociopolitical leaders and institutions to account.

JYE20.name: Maritime Governance Yemen
JYE20.description: Stakeholders of the Joint Programme on Maritime Governance, launched in 2020, work to re-establish the Yemen Coast Guard and, in turn, strengthen the criminal justice system with regards to investigations and prosecution of maritime crimes. With a view towards progressing port, maritime, and regional security, the aim is to improve Yemen Coast Guard capabilities and prevent further deterioration in terms of social stability, promote the flow of aid and trade, counter maritime crimes off the coast of Yemen, and avoid the possibility of post-peace agreement vacuums by supporting maritime law enforcement policies and measures. Programme initiatives support the implementation of international agreements and resolutions, and generate results that make contributions to SDG 16 acceleration and all 2030 Agenda pillars.

4SD00.name: Sudan Financing Platform
4SD00.description: Overseen by international and national stakeholders, the Sudan Financing Platform informs the design and architecture of fit-for-purpose initiatives that reflect the “New Way of Working” in Sudan. Platform action compliments national strategies and pursuits, as well as approaches aligned with SDG acceleration and 2030 Agenda achievement.

COV00.name: UN COVID-19 MPTF
COV00.description: The Secretary-General's UN COVID-19 Response and Recovery Trust Fund was a UN mechanism to address the unprecedented socio-economic threats of the COVID-19 pandemic, particularly for countries and populations most vulnerable to the pandemic. Based on the principle of global solidarity, the Fund was UN reform in action. Through fast and efficient financing, the Fund mobilized the UN's expertise and its global reach for rapid integrated UN responses, led by the Resident Coordinator, to support countries and safeguard their progress towards the SDGs. The fund is now completed. The latest narrative report can be found: United Nations Covid-19 Response and Recovery Fund Final Narrative Report (February 2023)

FCR00.name: Global Fund for Coral Reefs
FCR00.description: The first United Nations multi-partner trust fund dedicated to SDG 14, the Global Fund for Coral Reefs (GFCR) is an innovative blended finance mechanism stakeholders hope to use to mobilize $500 million US dollars in grants and investment capital to put towards coral reef ecosystem conservation and resilience, and strengthening services in reef-dependent communities.

GNU00.name: Generation Unlimited
GNU00.description: Productive and engaged youth are essential for progressing the Sustainable Development Goals and Youth 2030 outcomes, but investments in education, learning, and work opportunities for young people have fallen short—creating an urgent need to dedicate significant and targeted support for young people (aged 10 to 24) around the world. The GenU strategy leverages the strengths of a diverse network of partners to cut a trailblazing path no single partner could successfully pursue alone. All action under the GenU brand is integrated, localized, and comprehensive, with investment opportunities and financing structured around local responses that make good on all SDG and 2030 Agenda principles and aims.

JKH10.name: Disability Inclusion and GBV Services Joint Programme
JKH10.description: The Disability Inclusion and Quality Services for Survivors of Gender Based Violence (GBV) Joint Programme promotes the rights of survivors of GBV and people living with disabilities. The Joint Programme supports stakeholders in providing integrated and sustainable responses that improve the delivery of, and access to, inclusive and comprehensive protection-based services.

JXE00.name: JP Climate Security Mechanism
JXE00.description: The Climate Security Mechanism (CSM) is a joint initiative by the UN Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs (DPPA), the UN Development Programme (UNDP), the UN Environment Programme (UNEP), and the UN Department of Peace Operations (DPO). It aims to strengthen the capacity of the United Nations to systematically analyze and address the linkages between climate change, peace and security. The CSM Joint Programme works with partners to advance peace-positive climate action, catalyze climate-informed approaches to peace and security, and forge partnerships at all levels to exchange information and build the evidence base.

GNQ00.name: Equatorial Guinea MPTF
GNQ00.description: The Equatorial Guinea Multi-Partner Trust Fund supports an ambitious stakeholder agenda to unlock progress and opportunities that lead to SDG attainment. Fund action supports catalytic interventions laid out in the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework for Equatorial Guinea (UNDAF 2019-2023) and national Socio-economic Response Plan (SERP). Contributions help partners rebuild in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic and establish a more resilient, equitable and inclusive society in Equatorial Guinea that cares for the most vulnerable.

JBY10.name: JP Belarus SDGs
JBY10.description: In supporting the acceleration of the SDGs in Belarus, stakeholders of the Joint Programme Belarus SDGs focus on implementing nationalized and localized initiatives that leverage comparative advantages between partners, strengthen national capacities, raise public awareness for the Global Goals, and support local SDG acceleration, monitoring, and evaluation

JGE50.name: Joint Programme for Rural Development in Abkhazia
JGE50.description: Applying localized and human rights-based approaches, stakeholders of the Joint Programme for Rural Development contribute to improving the quality of life, socioeconomic, and natural resource conditions of rural populations, including people living with disabilities and minority ethnic groups.

JGT40.name: JP Guatemala Corredor Seco
JGT40.description: Increasing water and food security to strengthen the resilience of households in the Dry Corridor of Guatemala. Wielding an innovative approach, stakeholders of the Joint Programme Living Better in Guatemala prioritized food and nutrition, as well as community and climate change adaptation, in the Dry Corridor of the country. By providing support to local governance on issues of gender equality, cultural sensitivity, and climate variability, Joint Programme Stakeholders attempt to improve food and nutrition security and raise the resilience of local households.

JGT50.name: JP GTM Integral Rural Development in Ixil II
JGT50.description: Priorities of the Joint Programme for Integral and Sustainable Rural Development in Ixil include raising the resilience of local communities to withstand socio-economic, environmental, and climate-relator stressors. Stakeholders designed the programme on a foundation of biodiversity, natural resources, adaptive recovery, and risk management to better address multi-dimensional poverty, food security, access to quality health and education services, poor water and sanitation systems, and income inequality in Guatemala.

JGT60.name: JP GTM Comprehensive Rural Development in San Marcos
JGT60.description: Strengthening inclusive governance to advance rights-based, sustainable development. Stakeholders of the Joint Programme for Comprehensive Rural Development in San Marcos work according to a multi-sector, multi-dimensional and multi-level action model that puts people at the center. Interventions strengthen local governance and public institutions to better address climate change, socioeconomic and gender inequality, food insecurity, natural resource management, biodiversity, and disaster risk management with a view to sustainable outcomes.

JPH10.name: JP Philippines Human Rights
JPH10.description: Drawing on strategic partnerships and constructive engagement around human rights, joint programme stakeholders strive to improve the human rights situation in the Philippines, by providing support to assist national systems and institutions in fulfilling international human rights obligations and commitments.

JTN00.name: Promoting women and girls’ leadership in the socio-economic and health response to COVID-19 in Tunisia.

AFG00.name: Special Trust Fund for Afghanistan
